tldr: Backprop for compound AI systems: every text variable — prompt, code, answer, SMILES, dose weight — is a parameter, and an LLM emits natural-language criticism at each edge that is chained backward and applied by a textual-gradient-descent step.
method: Wraps a compound system as a PyTorch-like computation graph v = f(predecessors), where variables are arbitrary text (system prompt, code snippet, an answer, a molecule SMILES, a radiotherapy importance-weight string) and functions are LLM calls, simulators, or numerical optimizers. The forward pass records each variable's predecessors; the objective may be nondifferentiable — unit-test results, an Autodock Vina docking score, or an LLM judge. The backward pass walks the graph in reverse topological order: for each edge an LLM gradient operator receives the successor's gradient plus the forward conversation and returns criticism of the predecessor (context concatenated with feedback), and feedback from all successors is aggregated, mirroring autograd through addition — which also yields minibatching via tg.sum. TextualGradientDescent.step then rewrites the variable from its accumulated criticism. The API mirrors PyTorch (tg.Variable, BlackboxLLM, TextLoss, loss.backward(), optimizer.step()), at most one gradient call per edge per iteration.
results: LeetCode Hard with gpt-4o, 5 seeds (Table 1): completion rate 0.26 zero-shot and 0.31 ± 0.012 for Reflexion run one-shot → 0.36 ± 0.018 for TextGrad, which used zero demonstrations.
Zero-shot question answering (Table 2): GPQA 51.0 CoT / 53.6 best reported → 55.0; MMLU-Machine Learning 85.7 → 88.4; MMLU-College Physics 91.2 → 95.1.

Prompt optimization for gpt-3.5-turbo with gpt-4o as the gradient engine (Table 3): Object Counting 77.8 CoT and 84.9 for DSPy BFSR with 8 demonstrations → 91.9 instruction-only; GSM8k 72.9 / 81.1 → 81.1; Word Sorting 76.7 / 79.8 → 79.8.

Molecules over all 58 DOCKSTRING targets: one PPARA run moves Vina -4.2 kcal/mol, QED 0.44 → -5.5 / 0.59 → -7.5 / 0.79 (Fig. 2a); across the 29 targets with approved drugs TextGrad matches clinical Vina and exceeds clinical QED, at median Tversky similarity 0.42 to the approved drug (range 0.14–0.90).

Prostate radiotherapy, 5 patients (Supp. Tables 1–2): PTV D95 hits the 70.20 Gy prescription (+0.00 ± 0.00 vs oncologist -0.10 ± 0.15) and mean dose is +0.51 ± 0.09 Gy over goal vs +1.97 ± 0.36 for the oncologist; rectum mean dose 23.88 → 17.18 Gy, bladder 22.39 → 20.92 Gy.
advantages: One fixed framework: the gradient operator and the TGD prompt are identical across all five domains — only the objective function and the graph change — so a new application costs a loss function plus a few lines of PyTorch-shaped code.

Extends the textual-gradient idea from prompt optimization to instance optimization, which the paper names as its advance over DSPy and ProTeGi: the artifact itself (code, answer, molecule, hyperparameters) is the parameter, optimized at test time without a training set.

Textual gradients are legible, so the edit carries its rationale: Fig. 1e's gradient finds the nums[i] == k edge case that breaks the first gpt-4o solution, and Fig. 3's gradients walk from 'increase the PTV weight' to 'slightly increase the bladder and rectum weights' as the tradeoff moves.

Complementary to program search rather than competing: it matches DSPy BFSR on GSM8k (81.1) and Word Sorting (79.8) with instruction-only prompts and no demonstrations, beats it by 7 points on Object Counting, and DSPy's demonstrations plus the TextGrad prompt reach 82.1 on GSM8k — while keeping test-time inference cheaper.
limitations: The authors' own §5 list: graph operations still do not cover tool use or retrieval-augmented components, and the molecule and radiotherapy results are in silico proof-of-concept — the ultimate test requires experimental and clinical assessment.

No convergence guarantee: variance reduction, adaptive gradients and LLM self-verification are named as future work, so nothing establishes that a textual-gradient step actually descends; gradients are unstructured text and can be noisy or uninformative.

Cost scales with the graph — up to one extra LLM call per edge per iteration plus the update call — and experiments are correspondingly small: 39 LeetCode problems, 12 prompt-optimization iterations at batch size 3, 10 molecule iterations per target.

Gradient quality rides on the critic model: prompt optimization uses gpt-4o to improve gpt-3.5-turbo, and the paper notes (citing prior work) that constraint-following reliability drops as natural-language constraints accumulate.
fits: Stage 2 (Optimization-as-Language) anchor: the general-purpose optimizer that later harness-search loops such as DGM, RRSI and Harness-Zero loosely analogize — they evolve whole scaffolds, TextGrad differentiates any text variable inside one. Pairs with DSPy as its sibling (program and demonstration search), OPRO and Promptbreeder as prompt-only ancestors, and Reflexion as the single-variable special case.
reading: Read §2 for the gradient operator, TGD.step and the general-case recursion (Eqs. 10–12); §3.1–3.3 for the code, QA and prompt numbers; §5 for the authors' own limitations. Skim §3.4–3.5 for molecules and radiotherapy.

High confidence.
